_about: SANITIZED RECONSTRUCTION, not a verbatim model reply. It stands for the first live Groq test of the release candidate (question below): three futures named exactly as the live draft named them (Launch and stay employed, Launch and quit job, Delay launch), each deciding the same two things by choices (keep or quit the current job; launch now or later), and number assumptions the user fills in. All other wording is written for this fixture. No personal data. It passes validateProposal, so a real reply of this shape is accepted the same way. Used by e2e/live-gaming.spec.ts and the unit tests; no request reaches a provider.
question: What if I started a small gaming company in Mumbai with ₹5 lakh in savings while keeping my current job initially?

proposal.interpretation: You want to start a small game studio in Mumbai, paid for from your savings, and to keep your job at first. I compared launching while employed, launching and leaving the job, and waiting before launching.

branches.name: Launch and stay employed
branches.description: Start the studio now and keep your current job while it grows.

branches.name: Launch and quit job
branches.description: Start the studio now and leave your job to work on it full-time.

branches.name: Delay launch
branches.description: Keep your job and save more before starting the studio.

variables.label: Current job
variables.why: Decides how much time the studio gets and whether a salary keeps coming in.

variables.label: When the studio launches
variables.why: Waiting gives time to save and plan; launching now starts the work sooner.

variables.label: Savings available
variables.why: How long the studio can run before it earns anything.

variables.label: Monthly studio costs
variables.why: Software, hardware, rent and other running costs.

variables.label: Monthly salary from the job
variables.why: Income that continues while you keep the job.

questions: How many hours a week could you give the studio while you are employed?
Does your employment contract allow side projects?
What would the first game be, and how long would it take to make?

formulas.label: Months the savings last
formulas.explanation: Only counts savings against studio costs; any income from games or the job is left out.

possibilities.text: Less time for the studio while the job continues
A steady income while the first game takes shape
Full days to work on the first game
Savings may run down before the game earns anything
More time to plan and to save before starting
The idea may lose momentum while you wait

missingEvidence: What your employment contract says about side projects
limitations: Game sales, platform fees and taxes are not modelled.
